newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia consumer spending seen firm in early '97.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia consumer spending seen firm in early '97.

text.p: Malaysian consumer spending is expected to remain strong in the first few months of 1997 amid steady growth in income and continued growth in the labour market, the national Bernama news agency reported on Thursday.

Quoting the Malaysian Institute of Economic Research's (MIER) quarterly report "Consumer Sentiments" for the fourth quarter of 1996, Bernama said the approaching Chinese lunar year and Eid al-Fitr festive celebrations in mid-February also portended strong consumer spending.

It said consumer sentiment remained optimistic in the last quarter of 1996, with the Index of Consumer Sentiment (ICS) totalling 129.5 points. This was slightly lower than the 129.9 points for the preceding quarter because of a slightly slower economic growth rate, it said.
The latest index was 2.5 points below the 132 recorded in the same 1995 quarter.
The employment index, which depicts consumer expectations about short-term employment opportunities, drifted down 6.7 points to 157 in the 1996 fourth quarter from 163.7 in fourth quarter 1995.

MIER said its latest survey suggested consumers are better off financially. Of the 1,240 households interviewed in Peninsular Malaysia in the last quarter of 1996, 24 percent said their financial income position had improved from six months ago.
Inflationary expectations continued to run high with a sizeable 85 percent of the households interviewed anticipating prices would rise inthe next quarter, MIER said.
